To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cognitive training is better for the cognitive functions, while client-centered, global cognitive stimulation is better for the language and ADL/IALD functions.
cognitive interventions are effective in improving the cognitive status of AD patients, and that the effects are dependent on the type of intervention and the functional area.
client-centered, global stimulation is better for the improvement of language functions, whereas cognitive training is better for the stabilization of cognitive and functional performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the use of cognitive therapy in mild AD is more efficient than cognitive stimulation alone.
the question of whether the cognitive stimulation is more effective than cognitive training and vice versa.
the question of which kind of cognitive therapy (client-centered global stimulation vs. working memory) leads to better cognitive and clinical results.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
client-centered, global cognitive stimulation is the more effective treatment.
the cognitive stimulation is more efficient than the cognitive training.

the combination of pharmacotherapy and cognitive stimulation is superior to pharmacotherapy alone and that the type of stimulation (cognitive stimulation vs. cognitive stimulation of working memory) depends on the functional area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cognitive treatment is more efficient in language processing and client-centered, global cognitive stimulation is more efficient in ADL/IADLI.
the cognitive therapy is more effective in improving cognitive functions and language processing and in increasing the subjective quality of well-being.

the cognitive stimulation of the client-centered, global type has the most beneficial effect on the cognitive and functional status of AD patients in general and is therefore the most suitable for the majority of AD patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cognitive stimulation can improve the quality of life in AD patients.
the choice of the cognitive treatment is crucial and that the choice of test is also important for the evaluation.
cognitive stimulation is a valid therapeutic option in mild AD.
